title: Clean up delayed commit timing
summary: Hesitation load points to delayed fire commitment after the target is already mostly acquired, which slows scoring even when raw aim is good enough.
why: Hesitation wastes already-correct aim by delaying the click or release decision.
Commit timing issues often feel like confidence problems, not mechanical inability.
actions: Run short blocks where you accept slightly lower accuracy in exchange for cleaner, earlier decisions.
Use a simple acquire -> commit -> fire rhythm and keep the cadence consistent for a full block.
Review whether hesitation appears more on small targets, after misses, or during target switches.
avoid: Do not solve hesitation by panicking shots earlier with no acquire standard.
Avoid stacking too much punishment after misses; it usually creates more double-checking.

drills.label: Commit drill
drills.reason: Commit-focused reps make delayed confirmation easier to spot and reduce.

evidence.claim: Hesitation is best targeted by cleaner decision timing, not only by more raw accuracy work.
evidence.excerpt: Hand-authored seed knowledge from the initial AimMod coaching model.
